title: RAG knowledge assistant with citations
tagline: Question answering over company documents with hybrid search, reranking, cited answers and a measured retrieval report.
pitch: I built an assistant that answers staff questions from a company's own documents and shows where every sentence came from. It searches two ways at once, by meaning and by exact words, then a second model re-reads the best candidates and puts the right passage first. If the documents do not contain the answer, it says so instead of guessing. I do not ask you to trust it: the repository has a retrieval report measured on a public benchmark and on a question set for the demo handbook, and you can rerun both with one command.
problem: Companies keep their knowledge in handbooks, procedures and manuals that nobody has time to read. Staff ask a colleague or guess. A plain chatbot makes things worse, because it answers from memory and invents details that sound right. A search box returns ten documents and leaves the reading to the user.
solution: A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) service for a fictional parcel carrier's operations handbook. Documents are split by heading into passages, indexed for keyword search (BM25) and for meaning search (embeddings in Qdrant). A question runs through both searches, the two result lists are fused, a cross-encoder reranks the top candidates, and the language model writes an answer only from the passages it was given, with a numbered citation after each claim. A relevance gate refuses questions the documents do not cover. An evaluation script measures each retrieval stage separately so the value of every component is a number, not an opinion.
features: Hybrid search: keyword search (BM25) and meaning search (embeddings) run together and their results are fused
Reranking of the best candidates with a cross-encoder model that runs on CPU
Answers with numbered citations that link to the exact document and section
Citation check: a citation that points to a passage the model was not given is removed and the answer is flagged
Refusal when the documents do not contain the answer, decided before the language model is called
A retrieval report comparing keyword, meaning, hybrid and reranked search on a public benchmark (BEIR SciFact) and on the demo handbook
An answer report: correct source cited, expected facts present, refusals on out-of-scope questions
A web page that shows the answer, the sources, and how each passage ranked at every stage
Runs with no API key: an offline answer writer and a tiny built-in embedder for the tests

stack.name: Python 3.12
stack.why: The standard language for AI work and the one every retrieval library supports first.

stack.name: Qdrant (local mode, qdrant-client)
stack.role: Stores the passage embeddings and finds the nearest ones to a question.
stack.why: The same client code talks to an embedded on-disk index or to a Qdrant server by changing one setting, so the demo needs no Docker and the production path needs no rewrite.

stack.name: fastembed (ONNX Runtime)
stack.role: Runs the embedding model (bge-small-en-v1.5) and the reranker (a MiniLM cross-encoder) on CPU.
stack.why: It gives the same models as sentence-transformers without PyTorch, so the install is about 230 MB instead of several GB and it starts fast on a small server.

stack.name: BM25 (own implementation, about 80 lines)
stack.why: Exact words such as error codes and product numbers are where embeddings fail. The code is short enough to read and has no extra dependency.

stack.name: Reciprocal rank fusion
stack.role: Merges the keyword list and the meaning list into one ranking.
stack.why: It uses only the rank positions, so there are no score scales to tune between two very different searches.

stack.name: OpenAI Chat Completions API
stack.role: Writes the final answer from the retrieved passages.
stack.why: The most widely supported format. The same code works with OpenAI, Ollama, Groq or Azure by changing one URL.

stack.name: FastAPI
stack.role: The HTTP API and the demo web page.
stack.why: Typed requests and responses and automatic API documentation with very little code.

stack.name: pytest
stack.role: Automated tests that run offline in seconds.

workflow.detail: Each Markdown document is split at its headings into passages of a bounded size. Every passage keeps its document title and section heading.
Each passage is indexed twice: its words go into a BM25 keyword index, and its embedding (a list of 384 numbers that captures meaning) goes into Qdrant.
The question arrives at the API. It is tokenised for keyword search and embedded for meaning search.
Both searches return their best passages. Reciprocal rank fusion merges the two lists into one list of candidates.
A cross-encoder reads the question together with each candidate and gives a relevance score. The candidates are reordered by that score.
If the best score is under a threshold, the assistant replies that the documents do not cover the question and the language model is not called.
The top passages are numbered and sent to the language model with the instruction to answer only from them and cite the number after each claim.
The citation numbers in the answer are checked against the passages that were sent. The reply carries the answer, the sources and a trace of every stage.

phases.name: Foundation
phases.goal: A repository that runs, with documents to search and a keyword baseline.
phases.outcome: A git repository with pinned dependencies, a 20-document operations handbook for a fictional parcel carrier (about 3,300 words), a splitter that turns it into 85 passages by heading, and a BM25 keyword index that answers in under a millisecond.

steps.text: Create the repo, virtual environment and pinned dependencies
Write the demo handbook: operations documents for a fictional parcel carrier
Split documents into passages by heading, with a size limit
Build the BM25 keyword index as the baseline

phases.name: Hybrid retrieval
phases.goal: Search by meaning and by keyword, fused and reranked.

steps.text: Embed passages with a CPU model and store them in Qdrant
Add a tiny offline embedder so tests need no model download
Fuse keyword and meaning results with reciprocal rank fusion
Rerank the fused candidates with a cross-encoder
Save the index to disk and reload it without re-embedding

phases.name: Cited answers
phases.goal: Answers written only from retrieved passages, with checked citations and refusals.

steps.text: Write the answer prompt with numbered sources
Add the OpenAI-compatible provider with token and cost tracking
Add the offline answer writer for tests and keyless runs
Check citations and flag answers without valid ones
Add the relevance gate that refuses out-of-scope questions

phases.name: Evaluation
phases.goal: Numbers for every retrieval stage and for the answers.

steps.text: Write the handbook question set with the correct passage for each question
Add a script that downloads the public BEIR SciFact benchmark
Measure recall, MRR and nDCG for keyword, meaning, hybrid and reranked search
Measure answers: correct source cited, expected facts present, refusals
Compare reranker models and keep the one the numbers support

phases.name: Interface
phases.goal: An API and a page a client can try.

steps.text: Build the FastAPI service: ask, search, documents, health
Build the web page with clickable citations and the retrieval trace
Add a command-line tool to index, ask and serve

phases.name: Verification and documentation
phases.goal: Proof that it works and a README a client can follow.

steps.text: Run the test suite offline
Run the project from a clean shell the way the README says
Run the answer evaluation on a real language model
Write the README with a diagram, real output and the results table
Complete the dashboard entry and check for secrets
